issues.failure_explanation: Counterexample to (i): $d=1$, $\Lambda=\Z$, $h=1$, $p=2$, $\mu=\delta_{1/2}\in V_1$: LHS $=1$, RHS $=1/4+1/4=1/2$. The proof's lower bound in (xbound) is false for skewed lattices (e.g. $\Z\times L\Z$, $x=(0.6,0)\in V_{(1,0)}$ has $|x|<\rad-|\lambda|$), the step $(a-b)^p$ vs $a^p-b^p$ is invalid, and the factor $\mu(V_{h\lambda})$ is dropped. The correct estimate from $|h\lambda|\le|x|+h\rad(V_0)$ is $\sum|h\lambda|^p\mu(V_{h\lambda})\le 2^{p-1}(M_p(\mu)+h^p\rad(V_0)^p)$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate (i) with the factor $2^{p-1}$ and prove it via $|h\lambda|\le |x|+h\rad(V_0)$ and convexity; adjust the finiteness computations accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.2(i) is false as stated; it is used only to show finiteness of $p$-th moments of $\mu_h$, $\nu_h$ in Theorems 4.1 and 5.1, which survive with the corrected constant (or directly from $W_p(\mu,\mu_h)<\infty$).
issues.title: Lemma 3.2(i) is false as stated (missing factor 2^{p-1}) and its proof is invalid
issues.why_classification: Local constant correction in an auxiliary lemma; all main theorems and rates are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then $\mu_h = \sum_{\lambda\in \Lambda} \mu(V_{h\lambda})\delta_{h\lambda}$ is an at most $N$-term approximation of $\mu$

issues.failure_explanation: The number of terms of $\mu_h$ is the number of fixed lattice cells $V_{h\lambda}$ carrying mass, which can exceed $\mc N(B_R,hV_0)$, the minimal number of arbitrarily placed translates covering $B_R$. E.g. $d=1$, $\Lambda=\Z$, $h=1$, $R=0.9$: $\mc N([-0.9,0.9],[-1/2,1/2])=2$ but the three cells $[-3/2,-1/2),[-1/2,1/2),[1/2,3/2)$ meet $B_R$, so $\mu$ with atoms at $-0.8,0,0.8$ gives 3 terms. Hence the claimed 'at most $N$ terms' is unproved and false in general with this $h$.

issues.failure_explanation: For $N<3^d\mc N$ the prescribed $h$ exceeds 1, but Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 4.1 are stated only for $h\in(0,1]$; in particular $(1+2/h)^d\le 3^dh^{-d}$ fails for $h>1$, so the term count argument does not apply in that regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $N\ge 3^d\mc N$ (equivalently $h\le1$) to Theorem 4.2, Corollary 5.2 and Corollary 6.2.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 4.2 and its corollaries are unsupported for small $N$ (below $3^d\mc N$).
issues.title: Theorem 4.2 stated for all N although its proof needs h ≤ 1 (N ≥ 3^d 𝒩)
issues.why_classification: Excluding finitely many small $N$ is a routine regime restriction that leaves the asymptotic rate and all constants intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then $\mu_N = \sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_N}\mu(V_{\lambda})\delta_{\lambda}$ is an at most $N$-term approximation to $\mu$

issues.failure_explanation: The Voronoi cells of $N^{-1/d}\Z^d$ are cubes centered at lattice points, so they are aligned with $[-1/2,1/2]^d$ only when $N=m^d$ with $m$ odd. E.g. $d=1$, $N=2$: cells $[-3/4,-1/4),[-1/4,1/4),[1/4,3/4)$ all meet the interior of $[-1/2,1/2]$, so $\mu$ with atoms at $-0.4,0,0.4$ yields 3 terms. For $N$ not a $d$-th power no $N$ congruent cubes tile the unit cube at all. The rate bound itself follows from Theorem 4.1, but the term count does not.

failure_location.quote: Setting $h=N^{-\frac1d}$ yields $N$ cubes of length $N^{-\frac1d}$ in the unit cube

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict to $N=m^d$ and use the aligned grid (odd $m$, or a shifted lattice $N^{-1/d}(\Z^d+\tfrac12\mathbf 1)$ with the same cell radius/diameter), or replace 'at most $N$' by 'at most $(\lceil N^{1/d}\rceil+1)^d$' terms.
issues.overall_effect: Corollaries 4.3 and 5.3 fail as stated for general $N$; the pixel/voxel interpretation requires alignment or a larger term count.
issues.title: Cells of N^{-1/d}Z^d do not tile the unit cube by N cells; 'at most N-term' claim false
issues.why_classification: The result must be restricted to perfect-power $N$ with aligned cells or accept a worse term count; a comparable result survives but the stated scope is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Notice first that this coupling sends $\mu$ to itself when restricted to sets in $B_R$.

issues.failure_explanation: $(I\times P_{B_R})_\sharp\mu$ is concentrated on the graph of $P_{B_R}$, whereas $\mu\times\widehat\mu$ is the independent product coupling; the two are different measures (equal only in degenerate cases). The proof of Theorem 6.1 correctly uses the graph coupling, so the misstatement is not propagated.
issues.overall_effect: A false displayed identity in the construction; no result depends on the product form.
issues.title: Coupling (I×P)_♯μ misidentified with the product measure μ×μ̂
issues.why_classification: Purely a mis-stated identity; removing it changes nothing downstream.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \item $f_\mu(x) \leq \frac{\eps^p}{ 3C \vert x \vert^{p+d+1} }$ where $C$ is the integration constant from integrating over concentric $d$-spheres,

issues.failure_explanation: $\int_R^\infty r^{-2}dr = 1/R$, which exceeds 1 when $R<1$; no lower bound on $R$ is assumed. Counterexample: $p=1$, $R=0.1$, $\mu$ with density exactly $\eps/(3C|x|^{d+2})$ on $B_R^c$ (mass $\eps/(0.6)\le1$ for small $\eps$) and the rest inside $B_R$; then $W_1(\mu,\widehat\mu)=\int(|x|-R)^+d\mu = \eps/0.6>\eps$ (the 1-Lipschitz test function $(|x|-R)^+$ shows the projection coupling is optimal), contradicting the theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume $R\ge1$, or replace the density bound by $f_\mu(x)\le \eps^pR/(3C|x|^{p+d+1})$ on $B_R^c$.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 6.1 (and hence Corollary 6.2) is false for $R<1$ under the stated density condition.
issues.title: Bound on I_1 uses ∫_R^∞ r^{-2}dr ≤ 1, which requires R ≥ 1
issues.why_classification: A one-line hypothesis adjustment restores the theorem with unchanged method and conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: For $j=\lfloor R\rfloor$ the term is $(1-\{R\})^{-2}$, unbounded as $\{R\}\to1$ (e.g. $R=0.9$ gives a first term $100$), so the sum is not $\le\pi^2/6$ and hypothesis (2) is too weak on the first shell. Counterexample: $p=1$, $R=0.9$, $\eps=0.005$, $\mu=\mu_\perp$ uniform on the sphere $|x|=1$: (2) requires $\mu_\perp(B_{(0,1]})=1\le \frac{0.005}{3\cdot 0.001}\cdot\frac{6}{\pi^2}\approx1.01$, satisfied, yet $W_1(\mu,\widehat\mu)=0.1>\eps$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $(j+1-R)^{p+2}$ in hypothesis (2) by $(j+1-\lfloor R\rfloor)^{p+2}$ (or assume $R\in\N$); then $(|x|-R)^p\le (j+1-\lfloor R\rfloor)^p$ on each shell and the series is exactly $\pi^2/6$.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 6.1 and Corollary 6.2 are false for non-integer $R$ under the stated singular-continuous decay condition.
issues.title: Shell sum ∑_{j≥⌊R⌋}(j+1−R)^{-2} ≤ π²/6 fails for non-integer R; Theorem 6.1 false as stated
issues.why_classification: A local strengthening of one hypothesis restores the proof with the same conclusion and scope.
